ei.title: Young Enough to Change the World

fullPassage:
Young Enough to Change the World

Many young people are making the world a better place. For example, Carter and Olivia Ries have become leaders in saving animals. Although they are only teenagers, they have actually made a difference in the world. How were they able to do that? Let's hear from Carter.

When I was five, my little sister Olivia and I each adopted a cheetah. Did we raise cheetahs at home? No, we donated to a charity that protects wild cheetahs in South Africa. Our parents told us that if we did not protect them, we might not be able to see cheetahs in the near future. We soon became interested in helping other endangered animals. A few years later, with help from our parents, we created a non-profit organization to protect them. We wanted the next generation to be able to see these animals, so we named our organization One More Generation. We also studied endangered animals and educated our friends about them.

Then one day, a terrible oil spill occurred in the Gulf of Mexico. A lot of sea animals were completely covered with oil, and they were dying. We had to do something. We started collecting animal rescue supplies such as pet carrying cages and rubber gloves from everyone in our neighborhood. Four months later, our family drove to the Gulf of Mexico to deliver what we collected and helped to save the animals. While we were working there, we learned something very useful. When we put mayonnaise into a turtle's throat, the turtle threw up. That way, we were able to get oil out of turtles. I never knew mayonnaise could be used to save animals!

On our last day, we met a marine life specialist. She told us that plastic waste is more dangerous to sea animals than oil spills are. A lot of sea animals and sea birds die from eating plastic waste. After we came home, we created an educational project about how to reduce plastic waste. In addition to this, our organization continues to do various projects to save animals. Although we started small, we are making a big difference. What you do today can change the world, so take that first step!

questions.stem: 본문의 내용과 일치하는 것은?
ch: 두 남매는 남아프리카에서 직접 치타를 길렀다.
Carter와 Olivia는 치타를 보호하는 자선단체에 기부했다.
성인이 되고 나서야 비로소 치타 후원을 시작했다.

det.korean: 5살 때 치타를 입양했지만 집에서 키운 것이 아니라 자선단체에 기부한 것이다.
det.analysis:
✅ ③ 자선단체에 기부: 'we donated to a charity that protects wild cheetahs' 일치.
❌ ① 직접 길렀다: 'Did we raise cheetahs at home? No' 부정.
❌ ② 10살 때: 'When I was five(5살 때)'.
❌ ④ 성인이 된 후: 5살 때이므로 성인 아님.
det.tip: adopt a cheetah = 치타를 입양하다(후원하다). 직접 키운 것이 아님.

questions.stem: 본문의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?
ch: 멕시코만에서 끔찍한 석유 유출 사건이 발생했다.
많은 해양 동물이 기름을 뒤집어쓰고 죽어가고 있었다.
정부 지원을 받아 구조 물품을 구입했다.

det.korean: 동네 사람들로부터 구조 물품을 모았다.
det.analysis:
✅ ④ 일치하지 않음: 정부 지원은 본문에 언급 없음.
✅ ① 일치: 'a terrible oil spill occurred'.
✅ ② 일치: 'completely covered with oil'.
✅ ③ 일치: 'from everyone in our neighborhood'.
det.tip: 정부 지원은 본문에 전혀 언급되지 않음.

ch: 석유 유출이 플라스틱 쓰레기보다 더 위험하다.

✅ ② 일치: 'plastic waste is more dangerous than oil spills'.
❌ ① 비교 관계 반대.
❌ ③ more dangerous이므로 차이 있음.
❌ ④ 플라스틱이 더 위험하다고 말함.

questions.stem: 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 가까운 __________에 치타를 볼 수 없을지도 모른다.
det.analysis:
✅ ① near future: '가까운 미래' 원문 일치.
❌ ② distant past: '먼 과거'.
❌ ③ same place: 시간 아닌 공간.
❌ ④ next country: 문맥 무관.
det.tip: in the near future = 가까운 미래에.

questions.stem: 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 단체 이름을 __________이라고 지었다.
det.analysis:
✅ ③ One More Generation: '한 세대 더' — 다음 세대도 볼 수 있기를 바라는 뜻.
❌ ① Save the Earth: 본문에 없음.
❌ ② Animal Friends: 본문에 없음.
❌ ④ World Wildlife: 본문에 없음.
det.tip: One More Generation = 한 세대 더.

questions.passage: Many young people are making the world a better place. Although / Despite they are only teenagers, they have actually made a difference in the world. How were they able to do that? Let's hear from Carter.
questions.stem: 다음 괄호 안에서 어법에 맞는 것은?

det.korean: 비록 그들은 십 대일 뿐이지만.
det.analysis:
✅ ① Although: 뒤에 절(they are only teenagers)이 오므로 접속사 적절.
❌ ② Despite: 전치사로 뒤에 명사(구) 필요.
❌ ③ Because of: 전치사구.
❌ ④ In spite of: 전치사구.
det.tip: 접속사(although) + 절(S+V) vs 전치사(despite) + 명사구.

questions.passage: She told us that plastic waste is more dangerous to sea animals than oil spills ①<u>are</u>. A lot of sea animals and sea birds ②<u>die</u> from eating plastic waste. After we came home, we created an educational project about how ③<u>reducing</u> plastic waste. ④<u>What</u> you do today can change the world.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: 플라스틱 쓰레기를 줄이는 방법.
det.analysis:
✅ ①are: 비교구문에서 동사 반복 적절.
✅ ②die: 주어 복수이므로 적절.
❌ ③reducing: 'how to reduce'가 맞음. how+to부정사 구조.
✅ ④What: 관계대명사 what이 주어 명사절을 이끔 적절.
det.tip: how to+동사원형 = ~하는 방법. how+~ing는 어법 오류.

questions.passage: No, we donated to a charity ①<u>that</u> protects wild cheetahs in South Africa. Our parents ②<u>told</u> us that if we did not protect them, we ③<u>might</u> not be able to see cheetahs in the near future. We soon became ④<u>interest</u> in helping other endangered animals.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: 멸종 위기 동물에 관심을 갖게 되었다.
det.analysis:
✅ ①that: 주격 관계대명사 적절.
✅ ②told: tell+간접목적어+that절 적절.
✅ ③might: 추측/가능성 조동사 적절.
❌ ④interest: 'became interested in'이 맞음. become+형용사(과거분사).
det.tip: become interested in ~(관심을 갖게 되다). -ed(감정 느끼는 주체) vs -ing(감정 유발).

questions.passage: Four months later, our family drove to the Gulf of Mexico to deliver (A)[that / what] we collected. I never knew mayonnaise could (B)[be used / use] to save animals!
questions.stem: (A)와 (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: 우리가 모은 것을 전달하기 위해. 마요네즈가 사용될 수 있다.
det.analysis:
✅ ② what — be used:
(A) what: 선행사 없이 명사절. what = the things that.
(B) be used: 마요네즈가 '사용되는' 대상이므로 수동태.
❌ ① that: 선행사 없으므로 불가.
❌ ③ use: 능동태 부적절.
❌ ④ that: 선행사 없으므로 불가.
det.tip: what(선행사 포함) vs that(선행사 필요). be used to+V(수동).

questions.stem: 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 거북이에서 기름을 __________.
det.analysis:
✅ ② get oil out of turtles: 원문 그대로.
❌ ① feed with oil: 반대.

❌ ④ protect from sharks: 본문에 없음.
det.tip: get ~ out of = ~에서 ...를 빼내다.

questions.passage: We wanted the next generation to be able to see these animals, so we named our organization One More Generation. We also studied endangered animals and educated our friends about them.
questions.stem: 다음 중 본문의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?
ch: 다음 세대도 동물을 볼 수 있기를 원했다.
선생님들에게 멸종 위기 동물에 대해 가르쳤다.

det.korean: 친구들에게 가르쳐 주었다.
det.analysis:
✅ ④ 일치하지 않음: 'educated our friends'(친구들)이지 선생님이 아님.
✅ ① 일치: 'named our organization One More Generation'.
✅ ② 일치: 'wanted the next generation to be able to see'.
✅ ③ 일치: 'studied endangered animals'.
det.tip: friends(친구들)와 teachers(선생님들) 바꿔치기 함정.

questions.passage:
Young Enough to Change the World

Many young people are making the world a better place. For example, Carter and Olivia Ries have become leaders in saving animals. Although they are only teenagers, they have actually made a difference in the world. How were they able to do that? Let's hear from Carter.

When I was five, my little sister Olivia and I each adopted a cheetah. Did we raise cheetahs at home? No, we donated to a charity that protects wild cheetahs in South Africa. Our parents told us that if we did not protect them, we might not be able to see cheetahs in the near future. We soon became interested in helping other endangered animals. A few years later, with help from our parents, we created a non-profit organization to protect them. We wanted the next generation to be able to see these animals, so we named our organization One More Generation. We also studied endangered animals and educated our friends about them.

Then one day, a terrible oil spill occurred in the Gulf of Mexico. A lot of sea animals were completely covered with oil, and they were dying. We had to do something. We started collecting animal rescue supplies such as pet carrying cages and rubber gloves from everyone in our neighborhood. Four months later, our family drove to the Gulf of Mexico to deliver what we collected and helped to save the animals. While we were working there, we learned something very useful. When we put mayonnaise into a turtle's throat, the turtle threw up. That way, we were able to get oil out of turtles. I never knew mayonnaise could be used to save animals!

On our last day, we met a marine life specialist. She told us that plastic waste is more dangerous to sea animals than oil spills are. A lot of sea animals and sea birds die from eating plastic waste. After we came home, we created an educational project about how to reduce plastic waste. In addition to this, our organization continues to do various projects to save animals. Although we started small, we are making a big difference. What you do today can change the world, so take that first step!
questions.stem: 윗글의 마지막 문장에서 글쓴이가 전달하고자 하는 메시지로 가장 적절한 것은?
ch: 작은 시작이라도 행동으로 옮기면 큰 변화를 만들 수 있다.
어른이 되어야 의미 있는 일을 할 수 있다.
큰 단체에 가입해야 세상을 바꿀 수 있다.
세상을 바꾸려면 반드시 해외로 나가야 한다.

det.korean: 작게 시작했지만 큰 변화. 첫발을 내디뎌라!
det.analysis:
✅ ① 작은 시작→큰 변화: 'started small → big difference' + 'take that first step'.
❌ ② 어른이 되어야: 'only teenagers'로 십 대도 가능.
❌ ③ 큰 단체: 스스로 작은 단체를 만듦.
❌ ④ 해외 필수: 한 사례일 뿐.
det.tip: started small + big difference + first step → 작은 행동의 큰 힘.

questions.stem: 마요네즈에 대한 본문의 설명으로 옳은 것은?
ch: 거북이 목구멍에 넣으면 구토를 유발하여 기름을 빼낼 수 있다.

det.korean: 마요네즈를 목구멍에 넣으면 거북이가 토해서 기름을 빼낼 수 있다.
det.analysis:
✅ ① 구토→기름 제거: 'put mayonnaise → threw up → get oil out' 일치.

❌ ③ 유출 방지: 이미 유출된 기름 제거.
❌ ④ 영양 공급: 본문에 없음.
det.tip: 마요네즈 = 구토 유발 → 기름 배출.

ch: 많은 젊은 사람들이 세상을 더 좋은 곳으로 만들고 있다.
Carter와 Olivia는 성인이 되어서 동물 보호를 시작했다.
Carter와 Olivia는 동물을 구하는 일에 리더가 되었다.
그들은 실제로 세상에 변화를 일으켜 왔다.

✅ ③ 적절: 'leaders in saving animals'.
✅ ④ 적절: 'made a difference'.
det.tip: teenagers = 십 대. 성인이 아님.

questions.stem:
다음 질문에 대한 답으로 가장 적절한 것은?

ch: The name was chosen to reflect their plan to start many more organizations.
Because they wanted the next generation to see the animals too.
Because their parents chose the name for them.
The name came from their goal to study for one additional year.

❌ ③ parents chose: 부모가 이름 지은 것 아님.
❌ ④ study one more year: 아님.
det.tip: One More Generation = 한 세대 더.
